related_cases: HCJ 2144/20 Movement for Quality Government in Israel v. Speaker of the Knesset (judgment 23 March 2020; further decision 25 March 2020, the date Versa gives; versa.cardozo.yu.edu/opinions/movement-quality-government-israel-v-speaker-knesset) applied s.20(a). It did not attack the provision, and the continuity rule for the outgoing Speaker that it also applied came from the 2016 amendment.
rows.note: Amendment 37 (passed 19.7.2006) replaced s.12 (first sitting within 14 days of the election on a date fixed by law), repealed s.13 and amended s.20(a) (the most veteran MK as acting Speaker; definition of 'most veteran').

related_cases: Wattad v. Knesset (High Court of Justice; filed about three weeks after the November 2010 statute; seven-justice panel under Deputy President Naor; order nisi November 2012; source en.idi.org.il/articles/6720). It attacked the ordinary 2010 referendum statute (the Law and Administration (Cancellation of Application of Law, Jurisdiction and Administration) (Amendment) Law, 2010) for not being enacted as a Basic Law, not this Basic Law. The docket number HCJ 9149/10 is from the reader's recollection and was not confirmed in any source read. The final disposition was not established.
rows.note: The Basic Law was enacted in March 2014 while the Wattad petition against the 2010 statute was pending. No source read shows that the petition was amended to attack the Basic Law, or any later petition against it. Because the petition's outcome is unknown, this row needs a Nevo or court-database check.

Prime Minister, Government of Israel and Attorney General (High Court of Justice petition dated 29.8.2024; docket number blank in the published copy, shakuf.co.il/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/עתירה-סעיף-40-לחוק-יסוד-הממשלה-סופי.pdf).
